facts.statement: Puertasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The genus Puertasaurus was described by Fernando Novas and colleagues in 2005.
facts.quote: Described by the paleontologist Fernando Novas and colleagues in 2005

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Puertasaurus was found in Santa Cruz Province, southern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype and only known specimen of Puertasaurus reuili was discovered in the Santa Cruz Province of southern Patagonia, Argentina

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered by Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil in January 2001.
facts.quote: named after the fossil hunters Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil, who discovered the holotype in January 2001 and prepared it afterwards

facts.statement: The discovery of Puertasaurus was announced in July 2006 at the Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences in Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: Its discovery was announced in July 2006, at the Argentine Museum of Natural Sciences in Buenos Aires

facts.statement: Puertasaurus was the first giant titanosaur discovered with preserved cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus was the first discovered giant titanosaur that preserved cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: The fossil record consists of four vertebrae: one cervical, one dorsal, and two caudal.
facts.quote: It consists of four well-preserved vertebrae, including one cervical, one dorsal, and two caudal vertebrae

facts.statement: The preserved dorsal vertebra is 1.68 meters wide, making it the broadest sauropod vertebra known.
facts.quote: The largest of the four preserved bones is the dorsal vertebra, which at 1.68 m wide is the broadest known vertebra of any sauropod

facts.statement: Current estimates suggest Puertasaurus was about 30 meters long and 50 metric tons in mass.
facts.quote: current estimates place it around 30 m long and 50 MT in mass

facts.statement: Two-thirds of the dorsal vertebra's width consists of heavily expanded transverse processes that form wing-like structures.
facts.quote: two-thirds of its width is made up of the huge transverse processes (structures projecting from the side of the vertebra), which are heavily expanded and have very deep bases, forming wing-like structures when viewed from the front

facts.statement: The preserved cervical vertebra has a transverse width of 140 centimeters, including the ribs.
facts.quote: The cervical vertebra was also notably large, with a transverse width of 140 cm (including the cervical ribs)

facts.statement: The neural spine of the cervical vertebra is one of the proportionately largest of any titanosaur.
facts.quote: This would make it have one of the proportionately largest neural spines of any titanosaur

facts.statement: Puertasaurus belongs to Titanosauria, the dominant sauropod group of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus is a member of Titanosauria, the dominant group of sauropods during the Cretaceous

facts.statement: Puertasaurus is a member of the clade Lognkosauria, which includes large titanosaurs like Futalognkosaurus, Patagotitan, and Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: It is a member of the group Lognkosauria, which includes several other large titanosaurs, including Futalognkosaurus, Patagotitan, Argentinosaurus, Notocolossus, Mendozasaurus, and Quetecsaurus

facts.statement: Puertasaurus lived in a humid, forested landscape during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: When Puertasaurus was alive, the Cerro Fortaleza Formation would have been a humid, forested landscape

facts.statement: Puertasaurus shared its habitat with other dinosaurs, including the large sauropod Dreadnoughtus, as well as reptiles and fish.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus would have shared its habitat with other dinosaurs, including another large sauropod, Dreadnoughtus, in addition to other reptiles and fish

facts.statement: While generally considered a stable member of Lognkosauria, a 2017 study found Puertasaurus to be one of the least stable members of the group.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus is generally recovered as a stable (a firm member of the group) lognkosaur, although in 2017, Carballido found it (along with Quetecsaurus) to be the least stable members of the group

facts.statement: Puertasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period in southern Patagonia.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus is from the Late Cretaceous Period of southern Patagonia.

facts.statement: Recent studies date the Cerro Fortaleza Formation, where Puertasaurus fossils were found, to between 76 and 70 million years ago.
facts.quote: More recent studies have stated that these deposits pertain to the Cerro Fortaleza Formation, which was dated to the Campanian or Maastrichtian (approximately 76 to 70 million years ago).

facts.statement: The Cerro Fortaleza Formation represents a terrestrial ecosystem.
facts.quote: The Cerro Fortaleza Formation represents a terrestrial ecosystem.

facts.statement: Evidence in the formation suggests Puertasaurus lived in a humid environment with high rainfall and a high water table.
facts.quote: The presence of paleosols and lignite suggests a humid environment with high amounts of rainfall and a high water table.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence indicates Puertasaurus inhabited a low-lying forested landscape with poor drainage.
facts.quote: Avulsion surfaces, histosols, carbonaceous fossil roots, and silicified wood all provide evidence of a low-lying forested landscape with poor drainage.

facts.statement: The scientific name of the species is Puertasaurus reuili.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus reuili

facts.statement: Puertasaurus belongs to the unranked family Titanosauria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Titanosauria

facts.statement: Puertasaurus is classified within the family Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: familia: Lognkosauria

facts.statement: The genus was named in honor of technician Pablo Puerta who made the discovery, and the species name honors Santiago Reuil who reconstructed a vertebra from about 60 fragments.
facts.quote: El género fue nombrado en honor al técnico del Museo Egidio Feruglio, Pablo Puerta, quien hizo el descubrimiento, y la especie reuili en el de Santiago Reuil, quien reconstruyó una vértebra a partir de unos 60 fragmentos.

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the province of Santa Cruz, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron encontrados en la provincia de Santa Cruz, Argentina.

facts.statement: Puertasaurus is a genus represented by a single species, Puertasaurus reuili.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus ("lagarto de Puerta") es un género representado por una única especie, Puertasaurus reuili.

facts.statement: Puertasaurus was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur that lived in the Late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 68 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: Este fue un dinosaurio saurópodo titanosauriano que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 70 y 68 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Sudamérica.

facts.statement: Only four vertebrae have been found: the ninth cervical, the second dorsal, and two mid-caudal vertebrae, all in a very fragmented state.
facts.quote: Solo se hallaron cuatro vértebras, la cervical 9, la dorsal 2 y dos medio caudales, y en un estado bastante fragmentado.

facts.statement: The giant dorsal vertebra measures 168 cm in width and 106 cm in height.
facts.quote: La gigantesca vértebra dorsal, mide 168 cm de ancho y 106 de alto.

facts.statement: The transverse processes of the vertebra are the widest known in any sauropod, even wider than in its relative Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: Las apófisis transversales de la vértebra, estas crestas o protuberancias laterales, son las más anchas conocidas en un saurópodo, siendo inclusive mayor que en su pariente Argentinosaurus.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Fernando Novas stated that the discovery shows giant titanosaurs survived almost until the mass extinction 66 million years ago, while contemporary sauropods in other regions like Madagascar and India were much smaller.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de Puertasaurus reuili demuestra que los titanosaurios gigantescos sobrevivieron casi hasta la extinción masiva de los dinosaurios, hace 66 millones de años, que marcó el fin de la Era Mesozoica, dijo el paleontólogo Fernando Novas, los saurópodos contemporáneos de otras regiones del planeta, como Madagascar e India, eran mucho más pequeños.

facts.statement: It is one of the largest known dinosaurs and extends the presence of giant sauropods to the end of the Mesozoic era.
facts.quote: Es uno de los dinosaurios más grandes conocidos y extiende la presencia de los saurópodos gigantes hasta finales del mesozoico.

facts.statement: At the time, Puertasaurus was perhaps the largest sauropod in the world.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus fue, en su tiempo, quizás el saurópodo más grande del mundo.

facts.statement: Its size is a subject of controversy because the fossil bones are enormous but very poor in both quantity and quality.
facts.quote: Su tamaño es tema de controversia, los huesos fósiles son enormes, pero son muy pobres tanto en la cantidad hallada como en la calidad encontrada.

facts.statement: Fernando Novas estimated the species measured approximately 35 to 40 meters long and weighed between 80 and 100 metric tons.
facts.quote: Novas estimó que la nueva especie medía aproximadamente de 35 a 40 metros de largo y pesaba entre 80 y 100 toneladas métricas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimates a length of 30 meters and a weight of 50 tons in his reconstruction.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul en su reconstrucción estima a Puertasaurus con una longitud de 30 metros y un peso de 50 toneladas.

facts.statement: Scott Hartman estimates a length of 27 meters and a weight of 60 to 70 tons, using the close relative Futalognkosaurus to fill anatomical gaps.
facts.quote: Scott Hartman, quien en su restauración esquelética de Puertasaurus, utiliza principalmente al pariente cercano Futalognkosaurus para llenar los vacíos anatómicos, estimando al fragmentario taxón con una longitud de 27 m y sugiriendo un peso 60 a 70 toneladas.

facts.statement: In 2017, José Carballido and colleagues estimated its mass at approximately 60 metric tons, which was lighter than the more complete giant sauropod Patagotitan.
facts.quote: En 2017, el paleontólogo José Carballido y sus colegas estimaron su masa en aproximadamente 60 toneladas métricas, que era más liviana que Patagotitan, un saurópodo gigante más completo.

facts.statement: In 2019, Gregory S. Paul estimated the mass of Puertasaurus to be in the size range of Patagotitan at 45-55 tons.
facts.quote: En 2019, Gregory S. Paul estimó que la masa de Puertasaurus estaba en el rango de tamaño de Patagotitan en 45-55 toneladas.

facts.statement: The largest vertebra in the holotype, believed to be the second dorsal vertebra, measures 1.06 meters high and 1.68 meters wide.
facts.quote: De las cuatro vértebras conservadas en el holotipo, la más grande es la vértebra dorsal, que se cree que es una segunda vértebra dorsal, mide 1,06 metros de alto y 1,68 metros de ancho.

facts.statement: This is the widest sauropod vertebra known, with two-thirds of its width formed by enormous transverse processes.
facts.quote: Esta es la vértebra de saurópodo más ancha que se conoce, y dos tercios de su ancho están formados por enormes procesos transversales

facts.statement: The cervical vertebra was notably large, with a transverse width of 140 centimeters including the cervical ribs.
facts.quote: La vértebra cervical también era notablemente grande, con un ancho transversal de 140 centímetros, incluidas las costillas cervicales.

facts.statement: These features would have given it one of the largest neural spines proportionally of any titanosaur.
facts.quote: Esto lo haría tener una de las espinas neurales proporcionalmente más grandes de cualquier titanosaurio.

facts.statement: Puertasaurus was scientifically described by Fernando Novas, Leonardo Salgado, and Federico Agnoli in 2005.
facts.quote: La descripción técnico-científica de Puertasaurus, fue escrita por Fernando Novas, Leonardo Salgado y Federico Agnoli en el boletín del Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales Bernardino Rivadavia en 2005.

facts.statement: The discovery of four vertebrae from Puertasaurus was made in January 2001 in Santa Teresita, Argentina, and was funded by the National Geographic Society.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento de cuatro vértebras del cuello y el lomo del Puertasaurus, hecho en enero de 2001 en la estancia Santa Teresita, en la zona del Lago Viedma, en la Patagonia, Argentina, fue financiado por la fundación internacional National Geographic Society.

facts.statement: The species name honors fossil hunters Pablo Puerta and Santiago Reuil, who discovered the holotype in January 2001.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus reuilli fue descrito por los paleontólogos Fernando Novas, Leonardo Salgado, Jorge Calvo y Federico Agnolin en 2005, y lleva el nombre de los cazadores de fósiles Pablo Puerta y Santiago Reuil, quienes descubrieron el holotipo en enero de 2001 y lo prepararon posteriormente.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of four disarticulated vertebrae representing approximately 3% of the skeleton.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MPM 10002, consta de 4 vértebras desarticuladas, la mayor parte de la novena cervical, la dorsal 2 completa y el centro de 2 caudales, aproximadamente el 3% del esqueleto.

facts.statement: Puertasaurus was the first giant titanosaur discovered that preserved cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Puertasaurus fue el primer titanosaurio gigante descubierto que conservó las vértebras cervicales.

facts.statement: Recent studies indicate the deposits belong to the Cerro Fortaleza Formation, dating to the Campanian or Maastrichtian stages.
facts.quote: Estudios más recientes han indicado que estos depósitos pertenecen a la Formación Cerro Fortaleza, que se remonta al Campaniano o Maastrichtiano.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests a humid environment with high rainfall and a high water table.
facts.quote: La presencia de paleosoles y lignito sugiere un ambiente húmedo con altas cantidades de lluvia y un nivel freático alto.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence points to a low-altitude forested landscape with poor drainage.
facts.quote: Las superficies de avulsión, los histosoles, las raíces fósiles carbonáceas y la madera silicificada proporcionan evidencia de un paisaje boscoso de baja altitud con un drenaje deficiente.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Puertasaurus within the clade Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: El siguiente cladograma muestra la posición de Puertasaurus en Lognkosauria según González Riga y colegas, 2018.

facts.statement: Puertasaurus belongs to the parent group Colossosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Colossosauria

facts.statement: Puertasaurus is classified within the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Puertasaurus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The neural spine was oriented vertically but extremely expanded transversely, suggesting powerful neck muscles.
facts.quote: La espina neural está orientada verticalmente, perpendicular al centro, pero dorsoventralmente, de arriba abajo, bajo, aunque está extremadamente expandido transversalmente, de lado a lado.

facts.statement: The vertebral centrum was especially compressed dorsoventrally with wide and deep pre- and postspinal fossae, indicating powerful neck ligaments and muscles.
facts.quote: El centro está especialmente comprimido dorsoventralmente. Las fosas pre y postspinal de la columna neural son anchas y profundas.

facts.statement: The specific formation and geological age of Puertasaurus remain debated due to inconsistent stratigraphic nomenclature in southern Patagonia.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, de qué formación se derivó y su edad geológica han sido discutidos, debido a la nomenclatura estratigráfica inconsistente de la Patagonia austral.
